summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring a gastrostomy tube and status post bypass reversal was admitted with acute onset of large-volume diarrhea (>9/day), nausea/vomiting with small blood specks after retching, and worsened abdominal pain near the G-tube with poor oral intake. Evaluation showed stable labs and reassuring abdominal exam; abdominal X-ray demonstrated no obstruction or free air. Stool testing was negative for toxigenic C. difficile and positive for norovirus, and she was managed supportively with IV fluids, serial electrolyte monitoring, antiemetics, gastric mucosal protection (IV then oral PPI with ranitidine and sucralfate), and analgesia transitioned from IV morphine to home liquid oxycodone as oral intake improved. Symptoms steadily improved with tolerance of a light bariatric diet (Stage 5) and decreased diarrhea; she was discharged home ambulatory with continuation of home medications, ondansetron as needed, dronabinol held pending outpatient follow-up, and plans for outpatient reassessment of mild proteinuria and bariatric surgery follow-up regarding potential future G-tube removal.
